title: Mohammed Shami Retires From Test Cricket, Ending 64-Match, 229-Wicket Career
excerpt: Shami announced his decision on November 6, exactly 13 years after his Test debut at Eden Gardens, saying he was leaving the white jersey but not its memories — and that he will continue in white-ball and domestic cricket.
body:
• Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, November 6, 13 years to the day after his Test debut.
  • He finished with 229 wickets in 64 Tests at an average of 27.71, with six five-wicket hauls and best figures of 6/56.
  • His last Test was the ICC World Test Championship final against Australia at The Oval in June 2023.
  • Reports say he will continue playing white-ball cricket, including the IPL and domestic cricket for Bengal.

Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, ending a red-ball international career that began at Eden Gardens in November 2013 and finished, in playing terms, at The Oval in June 2023.

The India fast bowler made the announcement on Friday, November 6 — exactly 13 years after the day of his Test debut — in a heartfelt social media post, according to MyKhel and Sportskeeda.

“Leaving the white jersey, but never the memories”

“I'm leaving behind the white jersey, but never the memories tied to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had just one dream — to do something for my country. Since then, every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback has taught me something,” Shami wrote, as quoted by MyKhel. “Test cricket has been more than just a format for me; it has been an incredibly special part of my life. Today, with a heavy heart and countless beautiful memories, I am deciding to retire from Test cricket.”

"“Leaving the white jersey, but never the memories” “I'm leaving behind the white jersey, but never the memories tied to it."

He thanked teammates, coaches, family and fans, and also the BCCI and the Cricket Association of Bengal, “who believed in my talent, gave me opportunities to grow and played an important role in my cricketing journey.”

“Even though my last Test ball on the field may have been bowled, the pride of playing for India will always live on in my heart. Thank you, Test Cricket,” the message concluded.

A career built on seam, swing and comebacks

Shami made his Test debut against West Indies at Eden Gardens in November 2013 and quickly established himself as one of India's premier fast bowlers. Known for his seam movement and reverse swing, he claimed 229 wickets in 64 Tests at an average of 27.71, with six five-wicket hauls and best figures of 6/56, both reports said.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfaKPcEymrL/

Sportskeeda noted he remains the fifth-highest wicket-taker among Indian fast bowlers in Test history. That standing captures his place in a generation that changed how India won Tests away from home: pace, not only spin, as the decisive weapon.

His last Test appearance came in the final of the ICC World Test Championship 2023 against Australia at The Oval. Sportskeeda reported he took four wickets across the two innings in a match India lost by 209 runs.

The long wait for a recall that did not come

MyKhel reported Shami had been among the wickets in domestic cricket but had been repeatedly overlooked by selectors for an India comeback, even as he held out hope of returning. In the ongoing Ranji Trophy season he had played three matches for Bengal and picked up 14 wickets, and he is also part of Bengal's squad for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, MyKhel said.

Friday's announcement closes only the Test chapter. Reports of his statement said he will continue to play white-ball cricket, including the IPL and domestic matches. For Test cricket, though, the decision is final and deliberately timed: a debut and a farewell on the same date, 13 years apart.

For diaspora fans who watched India's pace attack become a world force in Australia, England and at home, Shami's upright seam and late movement were a signature of that era. He leaves the format with numbers that place him among India's most effective fast bowlers — and with the distinction of having helped redefine what an Indian Test attack could do.
